description: The bar chart illustrates the negative log-probabilities of clinically relevant tokens generated by the Mistral-v0.2-Base model (light blue bars) compared to the same model after being fine-tuned on data from six distinct clinical specialties: Cardio (light orange), Gastro (medium orange), Infect (dark orange), Neuro (brown), Obstetrics (dark brown), and Pediatrics (darkest brown). The vertical axis, labeled “Negative log probability,” ranges from approximately -22 to -27, with lower values indicating higher model confidence (i.e., better prediction). The horizontal axis groups bars by “Per-specialty terms,” meaning each group corresponds to tokens relevant to a specific specialty (e.g., “Cardio” group contains tokens relevant to cardiology). Within each group, the light blue bar represents the baseline model’s performance, while the colored bars show performance after fine-tuning on each respective specialty. In general, fine-tuning tends to reduce the negative log-probability (improve performance) for tokens within the fine-tuned specialty — for example, in the “Cardio” group, the Cardio-fine-tuned model (light orange) performs better than the baseline, and similarly, the Neuro-fine-tuned model (brown) performs best within the “Neuro” group. However, fine-tuning on one specialty does not always improve performance on other specialties — for instance, in the “Cardio” group, the Neuro-fine-tuned model (brown) performs worse than the baseline. The chart visually demonstrates that fine-tuning on specialty-specific data improves the model’s ability to predict relevant tokens within that specialty, while potentially degrading performance on others, highlighting the trade-offs in domain adaptation for medical LLMs.
